ko.executive_summary: MediaTek Q3 revenue reached NT$168 billion, exceeding guidance with data center business positioned for growth. Samsung System LSI is retreating from automotive APs to focus on higher-margin chips, while India's semiconductor push and agentic AI are reshaping telecom and connected devices.
key_facts: Department of War committed $1.5 billion loan to Wolfspeed for national security semiconductor applications
Samsung System LSI exiting automotive AP market

implications.text: MediaTek's data center pivot and Samsung's retreat from automotive APs signal shifting focus toward higher-margin AI and infrastructure chips away from commodity automotive segments.
US government loan commitment to Wolfspeed underscores national security prioritization in semiconductor supply chain resilience.
India's semiconductor push and agentic AI adoption in telecom present new market opportunities for AP designers.

ko.counterpoint: Samsung's exit from automotive APs may create capacity gaps in regional supply chains if alternative suppliers cannot scale quickly.
